description: Encoded Vastu Shastra placement heuristics (consensus of practitioner sources; see docs/procedure.md). Each zone value is one of the named levels. Unlisted zones take default_level.

pooja.label: Pooja (prayer) room
pooja.traditional: Ishanya (NE) is the seat of Ishana; worship facing east or north is prescribed.
pooja.physics: An east/north-east room receives the low-angle morning sun (daylight with modest heat) and stays cool in the afternoon.
pooja.remedy: If relocation is impossible, place the altar on the NE wall of the room so the worshipper faces east or north; keep the room light-coloured and uncluttered.

kitchen.label: Kitchen
kitchen.traditional: Agneya (SE) is ruled by Agni, the fire element; NW (Vayu) is the accepted alternative.
kitchen.physics: An east-facing kitchen gets morning daylight during breakfast preparation and avoids coinciding afternoon solar and cooking heat loads.
kitchen.remedy: Place the cooking range in the SE corner of the kitchen so the cook faces east; keep the sink (water) away from the stove; ensure an exhaust on an outside wall.

master_bedroom.label: Master bedroom
master_bedroom.traditional: Nairutya (SW) is the heaviest, most stable quarter, assigned to the head of the household.
master_bedroom.physics: SW/W rooms carry the peak afternoon sol-air load; high thermal-mass walls in this quarter delay that heat (time lag) and protect the rest of the house.
master_bedroom.remedy: Keep the bed in the SW part of the room with the head to the south or west; use heavy furniture/wardrobes on the SW walls.

bedroom.label: Bedroom
bedroom.traditional: Children's and guest rooms are assigned to the west (Varuna) and north-west (Vayu).
bedroom.physics: West/north-west rooms receive diffuse daylight in the morning; shading the west facade controls the afternoon peak.
bedroom.remedy: Place the bed so the sleeper's head points south or east; avoid mirrors facing the bed.

living.label: Living room
living.traditional: Reception spaces belong to the light, open north and east (Kubera, Indra).
living.physics: North light is the most uniform daylight; east openings admit morning sun and allow evening cooling.
living.remedy: Arrange seating so that the host faces east or north; keep heavy furniture on the S and W walls.

dining.label: Dining
dining.traditional: Dining is placed in the west, adjacent to the kitchen.
dining.physics: Neutral; the main requirement is adjacency to the kitchen.
dining.remedy: Keep the dining area adjacent to the kitchen; diners should face east or north.

toilet.label: Toilet / bathroom
toilet.traditional: Wet, impure functions go to the west/north-west; the NE (sacred) and SW (stable) corners and the centre must be kept free of them.
toilet.physics: A toilet needs an exterior wall for cross-ventilation and drying; the NW receives the afternoon sun, which helps dry wet surfaces.
toilet.remedy: Keep the toilet dry and well ventilated with an exhaust fan; keep the door closed; place the WC so the user faces north or south.

staircase.label: Staircase
staircase.traditional: The staircase is a heavy element and belongs to the south/west, rising clockwise.
staircase.physics: A staircase block on the south/west acts as a thermal buffer against the afternoon sun.
staircase.remedy: If the staircase cannot move, make sure it rises clockwise and keep the space under it as storage, not a toilet or pooja.

study.label: Study
study.traditional: Study faces east or north (sources of knowledge and wealth).
study.physics: North/east windows give glare-free daylight for desk work.
study.remedy: Place the desk so the user faces east or north.

store.label: Store room
store.physics: Unoccupied, high-mass storage on the hot facades buffers occupied rooms.
store.remedy: Keep heavy items on the SW side of the store.

garage.label: Garage / parking
garage.traditional: Vehicles (movement, Vayu) go to the NW; SE is also accepted.
garage.physics: An unconditioned garage on a hot facade acts as a buffer zone.
garage.remedy: Keep the NE free of vehicles; park facing north or east.

open_space.label: Open space / balcony / courtyard
open_space.traditional: Openness, water and low ground belong to the NE; the SW should be closed and high.
open_space.physics: Open space to the N/E admits daylight and morning sun while a closed S/W screens the hottest afternoon radiation.
open_space.remedy: Keep the NE open and clutter-free; plant tall trees on the S and W instead.

utility.label: Utility / laundry
utility.traditional: Washing (air and movement) belongs to the NW.
utility.physics: Afternoon sun on the NW dries laundry quickly.
utility.remedy: Keep drains flowing towards the north or east.

water_tank.label: Underground water tank / borewell
water_tank.traditional: Underground water belongs to the NE (lowest point of the site).
water_tank.physics: A shaded, low NE location keeps stored water cooler.
water_tank.remedy: Keep the area around the tank clean and covered.

septic_tank.label: Septic tank
septic_tank.traditional: Waste belongs to the NW, never the NE (sacred) or SW (stable).
septic_tank.physics: Keep wastewater downwind and away from the potable water source.
septic_tank.remedy: Keep a minimum separation from any water tank or borewell.

circulation.label: Circulation
circulation.physics: A central circulation core enables stack ventilation.

entrance.traditional: Entrances in the north, north-east and east admit the auspicious morning energy; the SSW-SW-WSW padas are considered inauspicious.
entrance.physics: N/E doors open to the cooler, shaded side of the house in the afternoon; a S/W door admits hot afternoon air and glare.
entrance.remedy: If the door cannot be moved, shift it within the facade towards the auspicious end (towards E on a south facade, towards N on a west facade); keep it well-lit.
